extracted.intended_audience: graduate students, scholars, and researchers in media studies, communication, and cultural studies
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for reorienting mass communication research away from an effects/utility framework toward a cultural-studies, hermeneutic, and practice-centered approach that foregrounds power, technology, and social relations. Emphasizes conceptual, methodological, and political shifts for scholars and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin analysis from a cultural crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: With Dewey one must begin the analysis of mass communication from within a genuine crisis in culture, a crisis of community life, of public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus research questions on failures to realize associative and democratic principles in contemporary life; treat the 'crisis of community life' as the starting point rather than assuming stability. Anti-pattern: treating media as neutral information conduits without situating them within social breakdown or civic decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reformulate communication as action/interaction, not representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discard the view of language as reference, correspondence, and representation and substitute the view that language—communication—is a form of action—or, better, interaction—that not merely represents or describes but actually molds or constitutes the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies that examine how communicative acts constitute realities and social worlds rather than simply measuring accuracy or referential content. Anti-pattern: analyses that treat media as mirrors of pre-existing reality or that focus only on information transmission models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a hermeneutic aim—understand what others are up to
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of doing all this—of looking at the practices that organize communications, the concepts such practices presuppose, and the social relations they bring into existence—is a hermeneutic one: to try to find out what other people are up to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize interpretive methods that render transparent actors' concepts, purposes, and practices (e.g., close reading, ethnography, participant observation). Treat understanding another person or culture as akin to understanding a scientific theory by examining embedded practices and conceptual worlds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on practices that combine conceptions, technologies, and social relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication is an ensemble of social practices into which ingress conceptions, forms of expression, and social relations. These practices constitute reality (or alternatively deny, transform, or merely celebrate it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the nexus of ideas, expressive forms, and institutional/technological arrangements; 'unhinge the practice at each of the points' (conception, expression, social relations) to see how meanings and relations are produced. Example: examine how a broadcasting format encodes class relations as well as messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat technique/technology as vectoral, not neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique is vectoral and not merely neutral in the historical process. A building, its precise architecture, anticipates and imagines the social relations that it permits and desires. So does a television signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate media technologies for the social relations they enable or anticipate; consider design and format as active agents shaping social possibilities. Anti-pattern: assuming technology is merely a tool independent of social imaginaries and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze communication as expressive forms and structuring social relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication is at once a structure of human action—activity, process, practice—an ensemble of expressive forms, and a structured and structuring set of social relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In studies, integrate analysis of expressive content (symbols, narratives) with the institutional and relational matrices that produce and circulate them. Avoid separating message content from production/distribution contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate conflict over the production and allocation of 'reality'
rubrics_metrics.description: Reality is, above all, a scarce resource. The fundamental form of power is the power to define, allocate, and display this resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat access to means of representing the world (classrooms, journals, newspapers, broadcasting, film) as central analytic objects; map who commands these 'machineries' and how that shapes what counts as real. Example: study gatekeeping, censorship, and institutional ownership as struggles over reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate class, status, authority, domination, and power into analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not only class conflict in communication but status conflict as well... names to mention: experience, subjectivity, interaction, conflict, authority, domination, class, status, and power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restore Weberian emphases on authority and domination alongside analyses of class; explicitly examine status divisions within elites and how they affect cultural production and access. Anti-pattern: analyses that report class inequalities but ignore intra-elite status dynamics or access to cultural institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recenter 'culture' and dispose of effect/function frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural studies make up a vehicle that can alter our self-image... At the very least, this position entails recentering and thinking through the concept of culture relative to the mass media and disposing of the concepts of effect and function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move research framing away from utilitarian/effects models (attitudes, uses and gratifications, measurable 'effects') toward interpretive accounts of cultural meaning, practice, and ideology. Anti-pattern: privileging narrow 'effects' metrics as primary evidence of media significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deconstruct and redeploy the effects tradition rather than abandon methods
rubrics_metrics.description: To abandon the effects tradition does not entail doing away with research methods... this literature will have to be deconstructed, and reinterpreted and the methods and techniques of the craft redeployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep quantitative and formal techniques where useful but reinterpret their findings in a cultural-studies vocabulary; explicitly articulate with past research rather than discarding it. Example: use survey data to illuminate culturally meaningful practices rather than to prove universal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift scholarly self-image: prioritize originality, solidarity, and concrete achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: We would talk less about rigor and more about originality. We would draw more on the vocabulary of poetry and politics and less on the vocabulary of metaphysics and determinism. And we would have more of a sense of solidarity with both the society we study and our fellow students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value creative, contextually sensitive contributions and commitments to civic engagement as scholarly virtues alongside methodological soundness. Anti-pattern: valorizing technical rigor as an end in itself while producing abstruse, politically disengaged work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed theoretical imports in national social formations
rubrics_metrics.description: Voices must be embedded in and deeply connected with the lines of discourse and the canons of evidence and argument that are decipherable only within the social, political, and intellectual traditions of given national social formations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adopting theories (Weber, Marx, Hall, Foucault), ground them in the local historical, political, and institutional context rather than applying them wholesale. Anti-pattern: uncritical transplantation of foreign theoretical frameworks without accounting for national specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconnect media studies to debates over mass and popular culture
rubrics_metrics.description: This means connecting media studies to the debate over mass culture and popular culture... apply the anthropological or primitive society conception of culture to the life and peoples of industrial society: to the language, work, community life, and media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat popular practices, everyday life, and 'long revolution' processes (Williams, Hoggart) as central subjects; use anthropological sensitivity to everyday culture in industrial contexts. Example: study media practices in working-class communities as legitimate forms of cultural analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symbolic interactionism and pragmatist traditions to analyze subjective life and action
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural studies, on an American terrain, has been given its most powerful expression by John Dewey and by the tradition of symbolic interactionism... Park provided the most powerful analysis of mass culture... transplanted Weberian sociology in American soil within the pragmatist attempt to dissolve the distinction between the natural and cultural sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate approaches that analyze subjective meanings, interactional processes, and the pragmatics of everyday life; combine this with attention to larger patterns of domination. Anti-pattern: purely structural analyses that erase subjective, interpretive dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to ideology as a central analytic category (British/Hall influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: British cultural studies could be described just as easily and perhaps more accurately as ideological studies for they assimilate, in a variety of complex ways, culture to ideology... ideological studies are, in Stuart Hall's phrase, 'the return of the repressed in media studies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how media and cultural forms function ideologically to mask and sustain social orders; use ideological critique to reveal concealed structural fault lines. Example: interrogate how 'consensus' produced by media erases political difference by rendering deviants as normless.
